title: CLR/25/2013 of MOH. ARIF Vs MANOJ BHATNAGAR and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

Shri Jitendra Chaudhary, Advocate, present for the revisionist.
Shri Siddhartha Singh, Advocate, present for the respondents.
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
Heard.
(2) This revision is directed against the order dated
21.02.2013, passed by learned Judge Small Causes
Court/6th Additional District Judge, Hardwar, in SCC
Suit No. 11 of 2011, whereby said court has
dismissed the application 66C moved by the
defendants before the trial court, for the amendment
in the written statement.
(3) Brief facts of the case are that the
plaintiff/respondent no.1 Manoj Bhatnagar instituted
Small Cause Suit No. 11 of 2011, against the present
revisionist Mohd. Arif and four others namely Mohd.
Javed, Mohd. Iqram, Mohd. Nisar and Aurangjaib
(respondent nos 2 to 5) seeking eviction of the
tenants, recovery of arrears of rent and mesne
profits. The defendants filed their joint written
statement and contested the suit. They moved the
Amendment Application 66C to incorporate the pleas
that they are not joint tenants of the
plaintiff/respondent, and that they are separate

3
tenants of the plaintiff land lord.
(4) The trial court rejected said amendment on the
ground that defendants are retreating from the
admission made by them earlier in their written
statement as to their joint tenancy.
(5) Learned counsel for the revisionist referred to
the cases of Baldev Singh and Others vs. Manohar
Singh and Another (2006) 6 SCC page 498, and
Usha Balashaheb Swami and others vs. Kiran
Appaso Swami and others (2007) 5 SCC page 602,
and contended that the trial court has erred in law in
rejecting the application for the amendment in the
written statement. He further argued that the
defendants are at liberty to take inconsistent pleas or
to alter written statement, to substitute their pleas.
(6) Having gone through the aforesaid case laws,
this Court finds that the same are on different facts
and circumstances. In the present case, what is
relevant is that not only the joint tenancy was
admitted by the defendants in their joint written
statement, but also in their application filed under
Order 15 Rule 5 of C.P.C. (U.P amendment) and in
their reply to Notice given by the land lord under
section 106 of Transfer of Property Act, 1882, they

4
(defendants) had admitted their joint tenancy and
never pleaded that their tenancy was separate. Not
only this, the defendants appears to have filed earlier
Suit No. 75 of 2011 in which they sought prohibitory
injunction against the land lord, not to evict them
from the premises in question and in which also they
never took the plea that they had separate tenancies.
(7) In the above circumstances, taking note of all
the aforesaid facts, this court is of the view that the
trial court has rightly rejected the application seeking
amendment in the written statement by the
defendants. In the opinion of this Court, there
appears no illegality in the order passed by the trial
court.
(8) Therefore, this civil revision is dismissed
summarily. (Stay Application No. 1808 of 2013
stands disposed of).
(Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Dt.09.04.2013
N.P
